title: Raft Key-Value Store
tagline: Build a Raft-replicated key-value store on a deterministic simulated network, then prove its client history linearizable.
summary: A five-node Raft cluster that elects leaders with randomized timeouts, replicates a log with the AppendEntries consistency check, commits by majority under the current-term rule, and applies committed commands to a key-value state machine. Clients PUT and GET through the leader; every run is a pure function of a seed, so partitions, crashes, and dropped messages replay exactly, and a Wing-Gong checker verifies the recorded history against a register model.
youWillBuild: A replicated key-value store whose leader election, log replication, commit rule, and client reads survive partitions, crashes, and message loss on a seeded simulator, with a linearizability checker over the recorded history.

languageWhy.Java: Records make messages and log entries immutable by construction, the switch over MessageKind is exhaustive, and the simulated network from the Raft lessons carries over unchanged; Python and Go ports follow later.

skills: Persist currentTerm, votedFor, and a 1-indexed log with the section 5.4.1 up-to-date comparison
Elect a leader with randomized timeouts drawn from a seeded RNG and prove at most one leader per term over many seeds
Replicate a log with the AppendEntries consistency check, nextIndex/matchIndex, and follower truncation while Log Matching holds
Commit by majority under the current-term rule, apply to a key-value state machine, and check the client history for linearizability

prerequisites.title: Raft I: Terms, Leader Election, and a Simulated Network
Raft II: Log Replication and Commit

stages.title: Term, Vote, and the Log
stages.summary: The persistent state every Raft server keeps: currentTerm, votedFor, and a 1-indexed log with append, truncate, lastIndex, lastTerm, and the up-to-date comparison, on top of the provided deterministic clock, RNG, and network.

stages.title: Leader Election
stages.summary: RequestVote and its receiver rules, randomized election timeouts from the node's seeded RNG, majority counting, heartbeats, and stepping down on a higher term, with a many-seed test that asserts at most one leader per term.

stages.title: Log Replication
stages.summary: AppendEntries with the (prevLogIndex, prevLogTerm) consistency check, nextIndex and matchIndex per follower, back-off on refusal, follower truncation of conflicting suffixes, and the Log Matching property checked after every delivery.

stages.title: Commit, Apply, and Linearizable Reads
stages.summary: commitIndex advanced by a majority of matchIndex under the current-term rule, followers committing up to leaderCommit, a key-value state machine applied in log order, client PUT/GET through the leader, and a linearizability checker over the recorded history.
